To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Deep Learning techniques are very effective in building recommenders and can be used to create low dimensional distributed embeddings of heterogeneous sources such as users, items, texts and images.

1) the use of deep learning techniques in recommender systems has increased in recent years; 2) the most popular architectures are the MLP and CNN; and 3) the most common use of these techniques is to generate low dimensional representations of heterogeneous sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects of recommender systems.
learning distributed representation of users items and their interaction data.
learning distributed representation of users, items, and their attributes in a unified way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
deep learning has a lot to offer in the area of recommendation systems and it is a promising area of research.
the future of Deep Learning in Recommender Systems is promising and exciting.
the future of recommendation systems is going to be driven by deep learning techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework that combines the best of both worlds, the deep learning and the traditional machine learning approaches, and we show how to use this framework for recommendation.
the deep learning models are able to extract the underlying semantic information from the heterogeneous data sources and use it for recommendation.
Deep Learning is a very powerful tool to create embeddings that capture the semantic relationships in a heterogeneous data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fundamental architectures used in recommendation are the same as those used in computer vision.
Deep Learning architectures can be used to learn distributed representations of heterogeneous sources for building effective recommenders.
the fundamental concepts behind Deep Learning are not that difficult to understand.
